entry_state: Insurance cash, service and profit follow different schedules. Gross and reinsurance groups retain separate measurement, and general measurement distinguishes future coverage, incurred claims, risk adjustment and unearned margin. The two-year case now tests those components.
exit_state: The loss component is tracked within liability, not added again. Financing changes CSM release and revenue timing even with unchanged claims. Two differently profitable issued groups and their separate reinsurance now share one company balance sheet.
findings: The zero-rate base closes at cash and profit 40. Future-service deterioration consumes CSM before loss; reversal restores loss first and then CSM.
An incurred-claim revision uses LIC rather than future-service CSM. The unreversed onerous path avoids treating all liability release as revenue.
The discounted path closes at cash 27.6; revenue 137.05 less finance expense 17.05 equals premium 120. Cash is explicitly uninvested.
Group B's loss and group A's margin remain separate, and reinsurance loss recovery is inside its asset rather than another receivable. No new defect observed.
